examples.translation: He knows himself well.

lessons.title: 便 and 一旦: a formal then, and once this happens
lessons.summary: 便 is a written equivalent of 就 that links an action to what follows, and 一旦 introduces a moment that, once reached, brings a result, usually with 就 or 便 in the next clause.
pattern: 一旦 + condition，(S) + 就 / 便 + result
body: 便 (biàn) works like 就 but sounds written or formal: 他吃完饭便出门了, 休息了一会儿，便又开始工作了. Like 就 it stands after the subject, right before the verb. 一旦 (yídàn) means once or in case: it marks a change that has not yet happened or that comes suddenly, and the next clause says what follows: 一旦下雨，比赛就要取消, 习惯一旦养成，就很难改了.

The contrast example uses 就 in the everyday frame 一……就……: 她一下课就去食堂吃饭了. 一 there means as soon as and describes two quick events in a row; it is not a condition, so 一旦 cannot take its place. A common mistake is to read 一旦 as one day: it means once or if ever, and what follows it is a condition, not a date.

examples.reading: tā chī wán fàn biàn chūmén le.
examples.translation: He went out as soon as he had eaten.

examples.text: 一旦下雨，比赛就要取消。
examples.reading: yídàn xià yǔ, bǐsài jiù yào qǔxiāo.
examples.translation: If it rains, the match will be called off.

examples.text: 这种习惯一旦养成，就很难改了。
examples.reading: zhè zhǒng xíguàn yídàn yǎngchéng, jiù hěn nán gǎi le.
examples.translation: Once a habit like this has formed, it is hard to change.

examples.reading: tiān yí liàng, wǒmen biàn chūfā le.
examples.translation: We set off as soon as it got light.

examples.text: 大家休息了一会儿，便又开始工作了。
examples.reading: dàjiā xiūxi le yíhuìr, biàn yòu kāishǐ gōngzuò le.
examples.translation: Everyone rested for a while and then went back to work.

examples.text: 她一下课就去食堂吃饭了。
examples.reading: tā yí xià kè jiù qù shítáng chī fàn le.
examples.translation: As soon as class was over, she went to the canteen to eat.

lessons.title: 似乎 and 仿佛: it seems, and as if
lessons.summary: 似乎 gives a cautious judgment (it seems), while 仿佛 compares with something imagined (as if) and is often closed by 一样 or 似的.
pattern: S + 仿佛 + clause / N + (一样 / 似的)
body: 似乎 (sìhū) softens a judgment: 他似乎不太高兴, 这件事似乎跟他没有关系. It is a more written 好像 and needs a verb or an adjective after it. 仿佛 (fǎngfú) is as if, for vivid comparisons and impressions; it can be followed by a noun or a clause and is often closed by 一样 or 似的: 仿佛一个孩子一样, 仿佛就发生在昨天.

The contrast example uses 似的, a particle at the end of the comparison (像……似的), not an adverb before the verb. 似乎 and 似的 share a character but sit in different places. A common mistake is to put a bare noun after 似乎: 似乎一个孩子 is wrong; say 仿佛一个孩子 or 像个孩子似的.

examples.reading: tā sìhū bú tài gāoxìng.
examples.translation: He doesn't seem very happy.

examples.text: 这件事似乎跟他没有关系。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì sìhū gēn tā méiyǒu guānxi.
examples.translation: This seems to have nothing to do with him.

examples.text: 听了这话，他似乎明白了什么。
examples.reading: tīng le zhè huà, tā sìhū míngbai le shénme.
examples.translation: Hearing this, he seemed to understand something.

examples.text: 那天的事仿佛就发生在昨天。
examples.reading: nà tiān de shì fǎngfú jiù fāshēng zài zuótiān.
examples.translation: What happened that day feels as if it were yesterday.

examples.text: 她笑得那么开心，仿佛一个孩子一样。
examples.reading: tā xiào de nàme kāixīn, fǎngfú yí ge háizi yíyàng.
examples.translation: She laughed so happily, just like a child.

examples.text: 他饿得像好几天没吃饭似的。
examples.reading: tā è de xiàng hǎo jǐ tiān méi chī fàn shìde.
examples.translation: He was so hungry it was as if he hadn't eaten for days.

lessons.title: 居然, 果然, 反而, 简直, 白, 刚好: against or in line with expectations
lessons.summary: 居然 marks a surprise, 果然 says things turned out as predicted, 反而 gives the opposite of what you would expect, 简直 exaggerates, 白 means in vain, and 刚好 means just right or by chance.
pattern: S + 居然 / 果然 / 反而 / 简直 + VP
V + 得 + 刚好 / S + 刚好 + VP
body: 居然 (jūrán) is surprisingly, against what you thought: 他居然十分钟就做完了. 果然 (guǒrán) is as expected, matching a prediction: 天气预报说有雨，果然下起来了. 反而 (fǎn'ér) is on the contrary, a result opposite to what the first part leads you to expect: 我想帮忙，反而给他添了麻烦. 简直 (jiǎnzhí) is simply, for exaggeration: 简直比饭馆的还好吃. 白 (bái) before a verb is in vain or for nothing: 白跑了一趟. 刚好 (gānghǎo) is just right or by chance: 你来得刚好.

The contrast example uses 当然 (of course), which says a result follows from common sense, while 果然 says it matches what someone predicted. A common mistake is to use 居然 for an expected result: 居然 always carries surprise.

examples.text: 这么难的题，他居然十分钟就做完了。
examples.reading: zhème nán de tí, tā jūrán shí fēnzhōng jiù zuò wán le.
examples.translation: Such a hard problem, and he finished it in ten minutes!

examples.text: 天气预报说今天有雨，果然下起来了。
examples.reading: tiānqì yùbào shuō jīntiān yǒu yǔ, guǒrán xià qǐlai le.
examples.translation: The forecast said rain today, and sure enough it started raining.

examples.text: 我想帮忙，反而给他添了麻烦。
examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng bāngmáng, fǎn'ér gěi tā tiān le máfan.
examples.translation: I wanted to help, but I only made more trouble for him.

examples.text: 他做的菜简直比饭馆的还好吃！
examples.reading: tā zuò de cài jiǎnzhí bǐ fànguǎn de hái hǎochī!
examples.translation: The food he cooks is honestly better than a restaurant's!

examples.text: 商店关门了，我们白跑了一趟。
examples.reading: shāngdiàn guānmén le, wǒmen bái pǎo le yí tàng.
examples.translation: The shop was closed, so our trip was for nothing.

examples.text: 你来得刚好，我们正要吃饭。
examples.reading: nǐ lái de gānghǎo, wǒmen zhèng yào chī fàn.
examples.translation: You've come at just the right time; we're about to eat.

examples.text: 他是北京人，当然会说普通话。
examples.reading: tā shì Běijīngrén, dāngrán huì shuō pǔtōnghuà.
examples.translation: He's from Beijing, so of course he speaks Mandarin.

lessons.title: 毕竟, 反正, 根本, 绝对, 的确, 可: taking a firm stand
lessons.summary: 毕竟 gives the deciding fact (after all), 反正 says the outcome is the same anyway, 根本 strengthens a negative, 绝对 is absolutely, 的确 confirms (indeed), and spoken 可 adds weight to a warning or denial.
pattern: S + 毕竟 / 的确 / 绝对 + VP
根本 + 不 / 没 + V; 可 + 别 / 没 + V
body: 毕竟 (bìjìng) points to the fact that settles the matter: 他毕竟还是个孩子. 反正 (fǎnzhèng) means anyway, whatever happens: 反正我已经知道了. 根本 (gēnběn) means at all and nearly always goes with 不 or 没: 他根本就没来过这儿. 绝对 (juéduì) is absolutely: 我绝对不会告诉别人. 的确 (díquè) is indeed, confirming what was said: 菜的确不错. 可 (kě) in speech stresses a warning or a denial: 你可别忘了, 我可没说过.

The contrast example uses 究竟 (exactly, in the end), which belongs in questions: 你究竟想要什么？ 毕竟 looks similar but makes statements, so it cannot replace 究竟 in a question. A common mistake is to use 根本 with a plain positive verb: 我根本知道 is wrong; say 我根本不知道.

examples.text: 别怪他了，他毕竟还是个孩子。
examples.reading: bié guài tā le, tā bìjìng hái shì ge háizi.
examples.translation: Don't blame him; he's only a child, after all.

examples.text: 你不说也没关系，反正我已经知道了。
examples.reading: nǐ bù shuō yě méi guānxi, fǎnzhèng wǒ yǐjīng zhīdào le.
examples.translation: It doesn't matter if you don't tell me; I already know anyway.

examples.reading: tā gēnběn jiù méi lái guo zhèr.
examples.translation: He has never been here at all.

examples.text: 你放心，我绝对不会告诉别人。
examples.reading: nǐ fàngxīn, wǒ juéduì bú huì gàosu biérén.
examples.translation: Don't worry, I absolutely won't tell anyone.

examples.text: 这家饭馆的菜的确不错。
examples.reading: zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài díquè búcuò.
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant really is good.

examples.reading: nǐ kě bié wàng le dài hùzhào!
examples.translation: Don't you forget your passport!

examples.reading: wǒ kě méi shuō guo zhèyàng de huà.
examples.translation: I never said anything of the sort.

examples.reading: nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng yào shénme?
examples.translation: What exactly do you want?

lessons.title: 自从: since a point in the past
lessons.summary: 自从 introduces a starting point in the past, and the main clause says what has been true from then on.
pattern: 自从 + past event / time (+ 以后)，S + ……
S + 自从 + event + 以后，……
body: 自从 (zìcóng) means since and always looks back to a moment in the past: 自从搬到这里，我每天都去公园跑步. The phrase often ends with 以后 or 以来, and the main clause often has 就, 都 or 再. It can stand before the subject or right after it: 他自从生病以后，就不再喝酒了.

The contrast example uses 从, which works for any starting point, including the future: 从明天起放假. 自从 is only for the past, so 自从明天 is wrong. A common mistake is to confuse 自从 with 从来 (ever, at all times, usually with a negative): 我从来没去过 is about never having done something, not about a starting point.

examples.text: 自从搬到这里，我每天都去公园跑步。
examples.reading: zìcóng bān dào zhèlǐ, wǒ měitiān dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
examples.translation: Since moving here, I've gone running in the park every day.

examples.text: 自从他去了国外，我们就很少联系了。
examples.reading: zìcóng tā qù le guówài, wǒmen jiù hěn shǎo liánxì le.
examples.translation: Since he went abroad, we've rarely been in touch.

examples.text: 他自从生病以后，就不再喝酒了。
examples.reading: tā zìcóng shēngbìng yǐhòu, jiù bú zài hē jiǔ le.
examples.translation: Since he fell ill, he has stopped drinking.

examples.text: 自从有了孩子，她的生活完全变了。
examples.reading: zìcóng yǒu le háizi, tā de shēnghuó wánquán biàn le.
examples.translation: Since she had a child, her life has changed completely.

examples.reading: cóng míngtiān qǐ fàngjià.
examples.translation: The holiday starts tomorrow.

lessons.title: 朝 and 沿（着）: facing toward, and along a route
lessons.summary: 朝 points to the direction a person faces or moves toward, and 沿 or 沿着 says a movement or a row of things follows a line such as a road or a river.
pattern: S + 沿（着）+ road / river + V
body: 朝 (cháo) is toward, the direction someone faces or turns to: 他笑着朝我走了过来. As a verb it means to face: 这个房间朝南. 沿 (yán) or 沿着 (yánzhe) is along, following the length of something: 沿着这条路一直走, 沿河种着很多树. 沿 alone sounds more written and goes before a one-syllable noun; 沿着 is usual in speech.

The contrast example uses 往 after a verb: 开往上海 (bound for Shanghai). 往 can follow verbs such as 开, 飞 and 寄 to give a destination; 朝 and 沿 cannot. A common mistake is to use 朝 for a route: you walk along a road with 沿着, not 朝着.

examples.reading: tā xiào zhe cháo wǒ zǒu le guòlai.
examples.translation: He came toward me with a smile.

examples.reading: wǒmen yánzhe hé biān sànbù.
examples.translation: We took a walk along the river.

examples.text: 这个房间朝南，阳光很好。
examples.reading: zhège fángjiān cháo nán, yángguāng hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: This room faces south and gets plenty of sun.

examples.text: 沿着这条路一直走，就能看到银行。
examples.reading: yánzhe zhè tiáo lù yìzhí zǒu, jiù néng kàn dào yínháng.
examples.translation: Go straight along this road and you'll see the bank.

examples.reading: yán hé zhòng zhe hěn duō shù.
examples.translation: Lots of trees are planted along the river.

examples.reading: zhè tàng huǒchē kāi wǎng Shànghǎi.
examples.translation: This train is bound for Shanghai.

lessons.title: 替, 同, 较: in place of, with, compared with
lessons.summary: 替 means doing something in someone's place or on their behalf, 同 is a more formal 跟 (with), and 较 is a written word for compared with.
pattern: A + 同 + B + V / 不一样
body: 替 (tì) is in place of or on behalf of: 我替你去开会, 请替我向你父母问好. 同 (tóng) as a preposition is a formal 跟: 我已经同他商量过了, 我的看法同你的不一样. 较 (jiào) as a preposition is a written 比, common in news and reports: 今年的游客较去年增加了一倍.

The contrast example uses 对, which marks the person an attitude is aimed at: 她对每个学生都很耐心. 替 says who you act for, 同 who you act with, and 对 whom your feelings or behaviour are directed at. A common mistake is to use 较 in casual speech; with friends say 比: 他比我高.

examples.reading: qǐng tì wǒ xiàng nǐ fùmǔ wènhǎo.
examples.translation: Please give your parents my regards.

examples.text: 你别担心，我替你去开会。
examples.reading: nǐ bié dānxīn, wǒ tì nǐ qù kāihuì.
examples.translation: Don't worry, I'll go to the meeting for you.

examples.text: 这件事我已经同他商量过了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ yǐjīng tóng tā shāngliang guo le.
examples.translation: I've already talked this over with him.

examples.text: 我的看法同你的不一样。
examples.reading: wǒ de kànfǎ tóng nǐ de bù yíyàng.
examples.translation: My view is different from yours.

examples.text: 今年的游客较去年增加了一倍。
examples.reading: jīnnián de yóukè jiào qùnián zēngjiā le yí bèi.
examples.translation: Visitor numbers this year doubled compared with last year.

examples.text: 她对每个学生都很耐心。
examples.reading: tā duì měi ge xuésheng dōu hěn nàixīn.
examples.translation: She is patient with every student.

lessons.title: 凭, 据, 依据: relying on, according to, on the basis of
lessons.summary: 凭 says what you rely on (a ticket, an ability, your effort), 据 introduces a source of information, and 依据 names the rule or fact a decision rests on and is also a noun for grounds.
pattern: 据 + source (+ 说 / 了解)，……
依据 + rule / fact + V; 有 + 依据
body: 凭 (píng) is by or relying on, for something that gives you a right or a result: 请凭身份证领取机票, 他凭自己的努力考上了大学. 据 (jù) is according to and introduces where information comes from, often as 据说, 据了解 or 据……说: 据他说，这家饭馆已经关门了. 依据 (yījù) is on the basis of a rule, a standard or a fact: 学校依据考试成绩给学生分班; it is also a noun, grounds or basis: 有什么依据？

The contrast example uses 用, which simply names a tool or means: 学会用筷子. 凭 is for something you depend on to earn a right or a result, not a tool in your hand. A common mistake is to use 据 for something other than information: 据了解 and 据他说 are fine, but effort or ability takes 凭: 凭自己的努力.

examples.reading: qǐng píng shēnfènzhèng lǐngqǔ jīpiào.
examples.translation: Please show your ID card to collect your plane ticket.

examples.text: 他凭自己的努力考上了大学。
examples.reading: tā píng zìjǐ de nǔlì kǎo shàng le dàxué.
examples.translation: He got into university through his own effort.

examples.text: 据他说，这家饭馆已经关门了。
examples.reading: jù tā shuō, zhè jiā fànguǎn yǐjīng guānmén le.
examples.translation: According to him, this restaurant has already closed.

examples.text: 据了解，这家公司已经有五十年的历史了。
examples.reading: jù liǎojiě, zhè jiā gōngsī yǐjīng yǒu wǔshí nián de lìshǐ le.
examples.translation: Reportedly, this company is already fifty years old.

examples.reading: nǐ zhèyàng shuō yǒu shénme yījù?
examples.translation: What grounds do you have for saying that?

examples.text: 学校依据考试成绩给学生分班。
examples.reading: xuéxiào yījù kǎoshì chéngjì gěi xuésheng fēn bān.
examples.translation: The school places students in classes based on their exam results.

examples.text: 这位外国朋友已经学会用筷子了。
examples.reading: zhè wèi wàiguó péngyou yǐjīng xuéhuì yòng kuàizi le.
examples.translation: Our foreign friend has learned to use chopsticks.

lessons.title: 以及 and 同: joining nouns and phrases in formal style
lessons.summary: 以及 adds a last item or group to a list in formal style, and 同 as a conjunction is a written 和 joining two nouns.
body: 以及 (yǐjí) means as well as. It joins nouns or phrases, often adding the last item of a list or a further group: 老师、学生以及家长, 工作计划以及其他问题. 同 (tóng) as a conjunction is a formal 和 between two nouns or pronouns: 我同他, 北京同上海. Neither of them joins two full clauses.

The contrast example uses 而且, which joins two clauses and adds a further point: 东西便宜，而且质量也好. 以及 and 同 cannot introduce a clause with its own 也 like this. A common mistake is to put 以及 between two sentences with their own subjects; use 而且, or simply start a new sentence.

examples.text: 会上讨论了工作计划以及其他问题。
examples.reading: huì shang tǎolùn le gōngzuò jìhuà yǐjí qítā wèntí.
examples.translation: The meeting discussed the work plan and other issues.

examples.text: 老师、学生以及家长都参加了这次活动。
examples.reading: lǎoshī, xuésheng yǐjí jiāzhǎng dōu cānjiā le zhè cì huódòng.
examples.translation: Teachers, students and parents all took part in this event.

examples.text: 我想了解这个城市的历史以及文化。
examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng liǎojiě zhège chéngshì de lìshǐ yǐjí wénhuà.
examples.translation: I'd like to learn about this city's history and culture.

examples.reading: wǒ tóng tā rènshi hěn duō nián le.
examples.translation: He and I have known each other for many years.

examples.text: 北京同上海都是大城市。
examples.reading: Běijīng tóng Shànghǎi dōu shì dà chéngshì.
examples.translation: Beijing and Shanghai are both big cities.

examples.text: 这家店的东西便宜，而且质量也好。
examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi piányi, érqiě zhìliàng yě hǎo.
examples.translation: This shop's things are cheap, and the quality is good too.

lessons.title: 从而, 可见, 假如, 总之: thereby, which shows, if, in short
lessons.summary: 从而 introduces a result reached through an action, 可见 draws a conclusion from evidence, 假如 introduces a supposition, and 总之 sums up what has been said.
pattern: 假如 + supposition，(S) + 就 ……; 总之，……
body: 从而 (cóng'ér) means thereby: the first clause is a method or an action, the second is the result it brings, usually for the same subject: 他坚持锻炼身体，从而保持了健康. 可见 (kějiàn) means this shows that, a conclusion the speaker draws: 他的房间一点儿也不乱，可见他平时很爱干净. 假如 (jiǎrú) is a formal if: 假如我是你，我一定会接受. 总之 (zǒngzhī) is in short or all in all, summing up: 总之，这次旅行让我很开心.

The contrast example uses 所以, the everyday so for cause and effect: 我生病了，所以没去上课. 从而 needs a deliberate action that leads to a result, so 生病了，从而没去上课 is wrong. A common mistake is to use 可见 for something that simply happens next; 可见 always introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said.

examples.text: 他坚持锻炼身体，从而保持了健康。
examples.reading: tā jiānchí duànliàn shēntǐ, cóng'ér bǎochí le jiànkāng.
examples.translation: He kept on exercising and so stayed healthy.

examples.text: 他提前做好了准备，从而避免了很多麻烦。
examples.reading: tā tíqián zuò hǎo le zhǔnbèi, cóng'ér bìmiǎn le hěn duō máfan.
examples.translation: He prepared in advance and thereby avoided a lot of trouble.

examples.text: 他连这么重要的会都忘了，可见他最近有多忙。
examples.reading: tā lián zhème zhòngyào de huì dōu wàng le, kějiàn tā zuìjìn yǒu duō máng.
examples.translation: He even forgot such an important meeting, which shows how busy he's been lately.

examples.text: 他的房间一点儿也不乱，可见他平时很爱干净。
examples.reading: tā de fángjiān yìdiǎnr yě bú luàn, kějiàn tā píngshí hěn ài gānjìng.
examples.translation: His room isn't messy at all, which shows he's usually very tidy.

examples.text: 假如我是你，我一定会接受这份工作。
examples.reading: jiǎrú wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ yídìng huì jiēshòu zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.translation: If I were you, I'd definitely take this job.

examples.text: 总之，这次旅行让我很开心。
examples.reading: zǒngzhī, zhè cì lǚxíng ràng wǒ hěn kāixīn.
examples.translation: All in all, I really enjoyed this trip.

examples.text: 我生病了，所以没去上课。
examples.reading: wǒ shēngbìng le, suǒyǐ méi qù shàngkè.
examples.translation: I was ill, so I didn't go to class.

lessons.title: 似的: like, as if, at the end of a comparison
lessons.summary: 似的 closes a comparison or an impression, usually after 像, 跟 or 好像: 像苹果似的 means like an apple.
pattern: 像 / 跟 / 好像 + N / clause + 似的
Adj / V + 得 + 像 / 跟 + …… + 似的
body: 似的 (shìde) is a particle that ends a comparison, usually opened by 像, 跟 or 好像: 红得像苹果似的, 雨大得跟倒水似的, 他好像什么都知道似的. After a clause it gives an impression of how someone acts: 她像没听见似的，继续看书. The whole phrase can describe an adjective, a verb or a person.

The contrast example uses 一样, which can do the same job (像……一样) but can also state real sameness before an adjective: 跟姐姐一样漂亮 means equally pretty. 似的 only gives a likeness or an impression, never equality. A common mistake is to put 似的 before the verb like an adverb; that is 似乎, which comes before the verb.

examples.text: 她的脸红得像苹果似的。
examples.reading: tā de liǎn hóng de xiàng píngguǒ shìde.
examples.translation: Her face went as red as an apple.

examples.text: 他好像什么都知道似的。
examples.reading: tā hǎoxiàng shénme dōu zhīdào shìde.
examples.translation: He acts as if he knows everything.

lessons.title: Four-character frames: A来A去, A着A着, 没A没B, 说A就A
lessons.summary: A来A去 is doing something back and forth or over and over, A着A着 is that while doing it something else happens, 没A没B means lacking any sense of A or B, and 说A就A means doing it the moment it is said.
pattern: V来V去 (back and forth, over and over)
body: A来A去 repeats a verb to show an action going back and forth or over and over: 走来走去, 想来想去 (after thinking it over and over). A着A着 says that while an action goes on, something else happens without warning, so it needs a second event: 听着听着就睡着了. 没A没B puts two related or opposite words after 没 to say something is missing: 没日没夜 (day and night, without rest), 没大没小 (no respect for age). 说A就A says the action follows the moment it is mentioned: 说走就走.

The contrast example uses 越来越, which also contains 来 but means more and more: 车越来越多了. It describes a growing change, not a repeated action. A common mistake is to stop after A着A着 with no second event; the frame needs a following clause, as in 说着说着，突然哭了起来.

lessons.title: 不得了, 用不着, 从……来看, (自)……以来: alarm, no need, viewpoint, time span
lessons.summary: 不得了 means terrible or a big deal, 用不着 means there is no need, 从……来看 gives the angle a judgment comes from, and (自)……以来 covers the time from a past point up to now.
pattern: 不得了了！; 没什么不得了的
从 + N + 来看，……; (自) + time / event + 以来，……
body: 不得了 (bùdéliǎo) on its own means awful or a disaster, often shouted with a second 了: 不得了了！ 没什么不得了的 means it is no big deal. (After 得 it is also a degree complement, 高兴得不得了, taught in its own lesson.) 用不着 (yòng bu zháo) means there is no need to, or I do not need it: 你用不着这么客气. 从……来看 means judging from: 从这次考试来看. (自)……以来 means since some point up to now, with or without 自: 自去年以来, 工作以来.

The contrast example uses 了不起 (amazing, impressive), which praises an achievement, while 不得了 warns of something serious. A common mistake is to use 以来 for a future time or a single moment: 以来 needs a span reaching up to the present, as in 工作以来，他从没请过假.

examples.translation: Oh no, the kitchen's on fire!

lessons.title: A的A，B的B; 由……组成; X也不是，Y也不是; X也X不得，Y也Y不得
lessons.summary: A的A，B的B divides a group into people doing different things, 由……组成 names the parts that make up a whole, and the two 也 frames describe being stuck because every choice is wrong.
pattern: X也不是，Y也不是; V1也V1不得，V2也V2不得
body: A的A，B的B divides a group: 大家唱的唱，跳的跳 means some sang and some danced. 由……组成 (yóu……zǔchéng) is to be made up of: 我们班由二十个学生组成. X也不是，Y也不是 says neither choice feels right, so you are awkward or at a loss: 站也不是，坐也不是. X也X不得，Y也Y不得 is stronger: you are not allowed, or cannot bring yourself, to do either: 打也打不得，骂也骂不得.

The contrast example uses 被, the passive marker: 这本书被他借走了. 由 introduces the parts of a whole, or the person in charge (由他负责); it does not mark something that happened to the subject. A common mistake is to drop 组成 and say 我们班由二十个学生; the verb must close the frame.

examples.text: 晚会上，大家唱的唱，跳的跳，玩儿得很开心。

lessons.title: Fixed formats: X是它，Y也是它; X着也是X着; 不管怎样说; 真有你的
lessons.summary: These spoken formats say one thing lies behind two outcomes, that you may as well use time you are wasting anyway, that a point holds whatever is said, and (真有你的) admiration or surprise at what someone did.
pattern: 不管怎样说，……; 真有你 / 他 / 她的！
body: X是它，Y也是它 names one cause for two opposite results: 这个手机，方便是它，麻烦也是它. X着也是X着 says you are idle or waiting anyway, so you might as well do something useful: 闲着也是闲着，不如帮我做点儿事. 不管怎样说 means whatever anyone says, the next point still stands: 不管怎样说，他也是你哥哥. 真有你的, 真有他的 or 真有她的 praises or teases someone for doing something clever, bold or surprising.

The contrast example uses 反正 (anyway), which also says the outcome does not change but gives the speaker's own decision, often a little impatient: 反正我不去. 不管怎样说 introduces a point that holds against every argument. A common mistake is to read 真有你的 as something you own; it is not about possession but about what the person has just done.

examples.text: 这个手机，方便是它，麻烦也是它。
examples.reading: zhège shǒujī, fāngbiàn shì tā, máfan yě shì tā.

lessons.title: Fixed formats: 哭什么哭, 什么钱不钱的, 不拿白不拿, 说来说去都是, 说什么就是什么
lessons.summary: X什么X tells someone to stop doing X, 什么X不X的 brushes a topic aside, 不X白不X says not doing it would be a waste, X来X去都是 sums up after much X, and V什么（就）是什么 means whatever is V-ed goes.
pattern: V + 什么 + V！; 什么 + X + 不 + X + 的
V来V去，都是 / 就是……; V什么（就）是什么
body: X什么X puts 什么 between two copies of a verb or adjective to tell someone off: 哭什么哭 (stop crying), 看什么看. 什么X不X的 dismisses a word the other person used: 什么钱不钱的 (never mind the money). 不X白不X says it would be a pity to miss a free chance: 不拿白不拿. X来X去，都是 or 就是 comes after doing something over and over and gives the bottom line: 说来说去，都是钱的问题, 找来找去，就是找不到. V什么（就）是什么 means whatever someone Vs is how it will be: 你说什么就是什么 (whatever you say goes).

The contrast example uses 什么 as an ordinary question word: 你周末打算做什么？ In X什么X there is no real question; the speaker is impatient and expects no answer. A common mistake is to use X什么X with people you should be polite to; it is blunt, so keep it for family and close friends.

lessons.title: 多项状语: stacking several adverbials before the verb in the right order
lessons.summary: When several adverbials stand before one verb, Chinese puts them in a fairly fixed order: time, adverbs such as 已经/都/也, manner of the doer, place, the person involved, then manner of the action.
pattern: S + time + 已经/都/也 + manner (of S) + 在 place + 给/跟/对 N + manner (of V) + V
body: An adverbial (状语) is anything that stands before the verb and tells when, where, how or with whom. A Chinese sentence often has several at once, and they do not go after the verb as in English. The usual order is: time (每天, 昨天), then adverbs of scope or time such as 已经, 都, 也, 常常, then a word describing the doer's attitude (很认真地, 很不高兴地), then the place phrase (在公园里, 在会议室), then the person the action is aimed at (给学生, 跟老师), and last a word describing the action itself (慢慢地), right before the verb: 她每天都很认真地给学生改作业.
Two short adverbs also have a set order: 也 comes before 都 (他们也都同意了), never 都也. A time word such as 每天 or 昨天 may also stand before the subject, so those examples accept two orders.

The contrast example uses 得: 她汉字写得非常漂亮. A phrase after 得 is a complement, not an adverbial; it comes after the verb and comments on the result. 地 marks a manner adverbial before the verb, 得 a complement after it.
A common mistake is to copy English order and put the place after the verb: say 我在图书馆看书, not 我看书在图书馆.

lessons.title: V不得 / V得: something must not or can be done
lessons.summary: V不得 says an action must not be done because it is harmful or improper (吃不得, 急不得, 说不得); the positive V得 says it is all right to do it.
pattern: V + 不得 (must not / cannot be done)
V + 得 (may be done; mostly in contrast or questions)
body: Putting 不得 (bu de) right after a verb says the action should not or cannot be done, because it would be harmful, dangerous or improper: 这种蘑菇有毒，吃不得 (it is poisonous, so you must not eat it). 这件事急不得 means the matter cannot be rushed. 这种话可说不得 warns that such words must not be said. The verb takes no object after 不得; the thing is named first, as a topic.

The positive form V得 (qù de) says the action is all right. It is less common and mostly appears next to the negative, in a contrast or in the question form V得V不得: 这个地方去得去不得. Several fixed words are built the same way: 舍不得 (cannot bear to part with), 怪不得 (no wonder), 恨不得 (would love to).
The contrast example uses 不了: 这么多菜，我一个人吃不了. V不了 says you are not able to do it (here, too much food to finish), not that you should not. Compare 吃不了 (cannot finish) with 吃不得 (must not eat).
A common mistake is to add an object after 不得: say 这个玩笑开不得, not 开不得这个玩笑 as an ordinary statement; keep the thing in front.

examples.reading: zhè zhǒng mógu yǒu dú, chī bu de.
examples.translation: This kind of mushroom is poisonous; you must not eat it.

examples.text: 这件事急不得，要慢慢来。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì jí bu de, yào mànmàn lái.
examples.translation: This can't be rushed; take it slowly.

examples.text: 他这个人批评不得，一说就生气。
examples.reading: tā zhège rén pīpíng bu de, yì shuō jiù shēngqì.
examples.translation: You can't criticise him; he gets angry at the first word.

examples.reading: zhège dìfang qù de qù bu de, nǐ xiān wènwen dāngdì rén.
examples.translation: Ask the locals first whether it's safe to go there.

examples.reading: zhè zhǒng huà kě shuō bu de!
examples.translation: You really mustn't say things like that!

examples.text: 这么多菜，我一个人吃不了。

lessons.title: 得不得了: extremely, terribly (after adjectives and feeling verbs)
lessons.summary: Adj + 得不得了, or a feeling verb + 得不得了, says a state or feeling is extremely strong: 高兴得不得了, 担心得不得了.
pattern: 心理动词 (feeling verb) + 得 + 不得了
V + O + V + 得 + 不得了
body: 不得了 (bùdéliǎo) after 得 is a degree complement meaning extremely or terribly. It follows an adjective (热得不得了, 紧张得不得了) or a verb of feeling such as 高兴, 担心, 喜欢, 想 (miss): 他担心得不得了. It is colloquial and emotional, stronger than 很 or 非常.
When the feeling verb has an object, repeat the verb: 孩子们想妈妈想得不得了, 她喜欢这只小猫喜欢得不得了. The object cannot stand between the verb and 得.
The contrast example uses 极了: 这首歌好听极了. 极了 also means extremely, but it attaches directly to the adjective without 得. So say 美极了 or 高兴得不得了, never 美得极了 or 高兴不得了.
A common mistake is to put 非常 after 得: 高兴得非常 is wrong; 非常 goes before the adjective (非常高兴).

examples.text: 听到这个消息，她高兴得不得了。
examples.reading: tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā gāoxìng de bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: When she heard the news she was overjoyed.

examples.text: 这几天热得不得了，大家都不想出门。
examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān rè de bùdéliǎo, dàjiā dōu bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.translation: It has been terribly hot these days, and nobody wants to go out.

examples.text: 孩子们想妈妈想得不得了。

examples.translation: The children miss their mother terribly.

examples.text: 他担心得不得了，一夜没睡。
examples.reading: tā dānxīn de bùdéliǎo, yí yè méi shuì.
examples.translation: He was worried sick and didn't sleep all night.

examples.text: 她喜欢这只小猫喜欢得不得了。

examples.translation: She absolutely adores this kitten.

examples.reading: zhè shǒu gē hǎotīng jí le.
examples.translation: This song sounds wonderful.

lessons.title: 下来 and 下去 for states: settling down, being handed down, carrying on
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 下来 marks a change into a calmer, slower or still state, or something kept from the past until now; 下去 marks carrying on from now into the future.
pattern: V / Adj + 下来 (become still or calm; past to now)
V / Adj + 下去 (go on, continue)
body: 下来 and 下去 also describe states, not only movement downwards. 下来 says something settles from movement or noise into stillness, slowness or darkness: 安静下来, 停了下来, 天色暗了下来. It also says something has been kept from the past until now: 爷爷年轻时的照片都保存了下来.
下去 says an action or state continues from now on: 请继续说下去, 你一定要坚持下去. With an adjective it says a bad trend goes on: 再这样瘦下去. So 下来 looks back from the past to now, and 下去 looks forward from now.
The contrast example uses 起来: 大家都笑了起来. 起来 says something starts, which is the next lesson's point; laughter that starts is 笑起来, not 笑下来.
A common mistake is to use 下去 for settling down: a room becomes quiet with 安静下来, and a car comes to a stop with 停下来. Keep 下去 for going on.

examples.text: 老师一进来，教室里马上安静下来了。
examples.reading: lǎoshī yí jìnlai, jiàoshì li mǎshàng ānjìng xiàlai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the teacher came in, the classroom went quiet.

examples.reading: chē mànmàn tíng le xiàlai.

examples.text: 爷爷年轻时的照片都保存了下来。

examples.translation: Grandpa's photos from when he was young have all been kept.

examples.text: 你说得很好，请继续说下去。
examples.reading: nǐ shuō de hěn hǎo, qǐng jìxù shuō xiàqu.
examples.translation: You're doing well; please go on.

examples.text: 学外语很难，但是你一定要坚持下去。
examples.reading: xué wàiyǔ hěn nán, dànshì nǐ yídìng yào jiānchí xiàqu.
examples.translation: Learning a foreign language is hard, but you must keep at it.

examples.text: 再这样瘦下去，你的身体会出问题的。
examples.reading: zài zhèyàng shòu xiàqu, nǐ de shēntǐ huì chū wèntí de.
examples.translation: If you keep getting thinner like this, your health will suffer.

examples.text: 听了这个笑话，大家都笑了起来。
examples.reading: tīng le zhège xiàohua, dàjiā dōu xiào le qǐlai.
examples.translation: Everyone burst out laughing at the joke.

lessons.title: 起来, 过来 and 过去 for states: starting, coming round, passing out
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 起来 marks a state or action that starts; 过来 marks a return to a normal state (醒过来, 明白过来); 过去 marks losing the normal state (晕过去, 睡过去).
pattern: V + 过来 (back to normal) / V + 过去 (out of normal)
body: 起来 after a verb or adjective says something begins and goes on: 天气暖和起来了, 两个人吵起来了. With an object, the object goes between 起 and 来: 外面下起雨来了. 起来 also has meanings learned as words: 想起来 (remember), 看起来 (look, seem).

过来 says someone comes back to a normal, conscious or correct state: 病人醒过来了, 他终于明白过来. 过去 is the opposite: someone loses that state, faints or falls asleep: 一位老人晕了过去, 他躺在沙发上就睡过去了. So 醒过来 but 晕过去; they are not interchangeable.
The contrast example uses 下来: 他的话让大家冷静了下来. 下来 says a state settles and becomes calm (previous lesson), not that something starts or recovers.
A common mistake is to put the object after 起来: say 下起雨来, not 下起来雨.

examples.text: 一到周末，这条街就热闹起来了。
examples.reading: yí dào zhōumò, zhè tiáo jiē jiù rènao qǐlai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the weekend comes, this street livens up.

examples.text: 两个人一见面就吵起来了。
examples.reading: liǎng ge rén yí jiànmiàn jiù chǎo qǐlai le.
examples.translation: The two of them started arguing the moment they met.

examples.reading: wàimian xià qǐ yǔ lai le.
examples.translation: It has started raining outside.

examples.reading: bìngrén zhōngyú xǐng guòlai le.
examples.translation: The patient finally came round.

examples.text: 他听了半天才明白过来。
examples.reading: tā tīng le bàntiān cái míngbai guòlai.
examples.translation: He listened for ages before it finally dawned on him.

examples.text: 他太累了，躺在沙发上就睡过去了。
examples.reading: tā tài lèi le, tǎng zài shāfā shang jiù shuì guòqu le.
examples.translation: He was so tired that he fell fast asleep as soon as he lay on the sofa.

examples.text: 因为太热，一位老人晕了过去。
examples.reading: yīnwèi tài rè, yí wèi lǎorén yūn le guòqu.
examples.translation: It was so hot that an old man fainted.

examples.text: 他的话让大家冷静了下来。
examples.reading: tā de huà ràng dàjiā lěngjìng le xiàlai.
examples.translation: His words calmed everyone down.

lessons.title: 得 + phrase: so … that (a verb phrase, a clause or a set phrase after 得)
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 得 can introduce a whole verb phrase, a subject-predicate clause or a set phrase that describes the resulting state: 笑得说不出话来, 讲得大家都笑了, 说得一清二楚.
pattern: V / Adj + 得 + set phrase (一清二楚, 要命…)
body: At HSK 2 the part after 得 is a simple adjective (说得很好). Here it grows. It can be a verb phrase showing how extreme the state was: 他笑得说不出话来, 她累得连饭都不想吃了. It can be a full clause with its own subject: 老师讲得大家都笑了 (the teacher spoke so well that everyone laughed), 外面冷得我直发抖. It can also be a set phrase: 说得一清二楚 (perfectly clear), 忙得要命 (terribly busy).
All three forms mean so … that: the first part names the cause, and the part after 得 shows the result or how far things went. Nothing else can stand between the verb and 得.
The contrast example uses 地: 她轻轻地关上了门. 地 marks how an action is done and stands before the verb; 得 stands after the verb or adjective and introduces the resulting state.
A common mistake is to put 很 or 非常 straight after the verb instead of 得: 他笑很说不出话来 is wrong; keep 得.

examples.reading: tā xiào de shuō bu chū huà lai.
examples.translation: He laughed so hard he couldn't speak.

examples.text: 她累得连饭都不想吃了。
examples.reading: tā lèi de lián fàn dōu bù xiǎng chī le.
examples.translation: She was so tired she didn't even want to eat.

examples.reading: lǎoshī jiǎng de dàjiā dōu xiào le.
examples.translation: The teacher told it so well that everyone laughed.

examples.reading: wàimian lěng de wǒ zhí fādǒu.
examples.translation: It's so cold outside that I can't stop shivering.

examples.text: 他把事情的经过说得一清二楚。
examples.reading: tā bǎ shìqing de jīngguò shuō de yì qīng èr chǔ.
examples.translation: He explained exactly what had happened, perfectly clearly.

examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān tā máng de yàomìng.
examples.translation: He has been terribly busy these days.

examples.reading: tā qīngqīng de guānshang le mén.
examples.translation: She closed the door gently.

lessons.title: 有着 and V有: formal 'has' and 'bears' (有着悠久的历史, 印有名字)
lessons.summary: 有着 + an abstract object says something has or contains a quality, history or feeling, in a formal style; V + 有 (印有, 写有, 画有) says something is printed, written or drawn on a surface.
pattern: place + V (印 / 写 / 画 / 刻) + 有 + object
body: 有着 (yǒuzhe) is a formal, written way to say has, mostly with abstract and weighty objects: history, friendship, feelings, dreams, differences. 这座城市有着两千多年的历史. The object usually has a modifier with 的; 有着 is not used for everyday things (say 我有一辆车, not 我有着一辆车), and it has no negative form with 没.
V + 有 says something is attached to or marked on a surface: 杯子上印有学校的名字, 信封上写有收信人的地址. The sentence starts with the place (杯子上, 信封上). It is formal, typical of notices and descriptions.
The contrast example uses V着: 台上坐着几位老师. V着 is the everyday sentence of existence (HSK 2–3) and works with any posture or placement verb; V有 is formal and used for writing, printing and similar marks.
A common mistake is to use 有着 with a concrete, simple object or with a number alone: 他有着两个哥哥 sounds wrong; say 他有两个哥哥.

examples.text: 这座城市有着两千多年的历史。
examples.reading: zhè zuò chéngshì yǒuzhe liǎng qiān duō nián de lìshǐ.
examples.translation: This city has a history of more than two thousand years.

examples.text: 这两个人之间有着很深的感情。
examples.reading: zhè liǎng ge rén zhījiān yǒuzhe hěn shēn de gǎnqíng.
examples.translation: There is a deep bond between these two people.

examples.text: 每个人都有着自己的梦想。
examples.reading: měi ge rén dōu yǒuzhe zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
examples.translation: Everyone has a dream of their own.

examples.text: 杯子上印有学校的名字。
examples.reading: bēizi shang yìn yǒu xuéxiào de míngzi.
examples.translation: The school's name is printed on the cup.

examples.text: 信封上写有收信人的地址。
examples.reading: xìnfēng shang xiě yǒu shōuxìnrén de dìzhǐ.
examples.translation: The recipient's address is written on the envelope.

examples.reading: tái shang zuò zhe jǐ wèi lǎoshī.
examples.translation: Several teachers are sitting on the stage.

lessons.title: 把 + O + 一 + V (a quick gesture) and 把 + O1 + V + O2
lessons.summary: 把 + O + 一 + V describes a quick, sudden movement, usually followed by what happens next; 把 + O1 + V + O2 lets the verb keep a second object, such as the person told or the part removed.
pattern: S + 把 + O + 一 + V，(就) + result
S + 把 + O1 + V (了) + O2
body: In 把 + O + 一 + V, the 一 makes the verb a short, sudden act, often a gesture: 他把门一关 (he shut the door, just like that), 妈妈把眼睛一瞪, 他把手一挥. The verb is a bare single verb with no 了, and the sentence almost always goes on to say what followed: 他把手一挥，大家就安静了.

In 把 + O1 + V + O2, the verb still has an object after it. O2 can be the person who receives something (把这件事告诉了经理, 把这个好消息告诉大家) or the part or result affected (把橘子剥了皮, she peeled the orange). O1 is what is handled; O2 completes the verb.
The contrast example uses 在: 请把车停在门口. This is the basic 把 sentence with a place after the verb (HSK 3), where the object ends up in a place; 在 is not a second object.
A common mistake is to add 了 to the quick-gesture form: 他把门一关了 is wrong; the 一 already marks the action as instant.

examples.text: 他把门一关，就躺到了床上。
examples.reading: tā bǎ mén yì guān, jiù tǎng dào le chuáng shang.
examples.translation: He shut the door and lay down on the bed.

examples.text: 妈妈把眼睛一瞪，孩子马上不说话了。
examples.reading: māma bǎ yǎnjing yí dèng, háizi mǎshàng bù shuōhuà le.
examples.translation: Mum just glared, and the child fell silent at once.

examples.text: 他把手一挥，大家就安静了。
examples.reading: tā bǎ shǒu yì huī, dàjiā jiù ānjìng le.
examples.translation: He gave a wave of his hand and everyone went quiet.

examples.text: 我已经把这件事告诉了经理。
examples.reading: wǒ yǐjīng bǎ zhè jiàn shì gàosu le jīnglǐ.
examples.translation: I've already told the manager about this.

examples.text: 你把这个好消息告诉大家吧。
examples.reading: nǐ bǎ zhège hǎo xiāoxi gàosu dàjiā ba.
examples.translation: Go and tell everyone the good news.

examples.text: 妈妈把橘子剥了皮，递给我。
examples.reading: māma bǎ júzi bāo le pí, dì gěi wǒ.
examples.translation: Mum peeled the orange and handed it to me.

examples.reading: qǐng bǎ chē tíng zài ménkǒu.
examples.translation: Please park the car at the entrance.

lessons.title: Serial verbs with cause, contrast or condition: 生病没来, 有钱不花, 有问题问我
lessons.summary: Two verb phrases can follow each other with no linking word and still mean cause (生病没来), contrast (有车不开) or condition (有问题可以问我); context gives the relation.
pattern: V1 (cause) + V2 (result): 生病没来上课
有 + N + 不 + V (contrast): 有车不开
有 + N + V2 (condition): 有问题问我
body: At HSK 2 two verbs in a row mean purpose or means (坐地铁去机场). Here the same structure carries other relations. Cause: 他有事没来开会 (he had something on, so he didn't come). Contrast: 她有车不开 (she has a car but doesn't drive it), 他借了钱不还 (he borrowed money and won't pay it back). Condition: 你有问题可以随时问我 (if you have questions, ask me), 有空来我家玩儿吧.
No 因为, 但是 or 如果 is needed; the order of events and the meaning of the verbs show the relation. The first verb phrase comes first in time or logic, so the two parts cannot swap.
The contrast example uses the basic serial pattern: 他坐地铁去机场. The first verb is the means and the second the purpose; there is no cause, contrast or condition.
A common mistake is to add a comma and a conjunction where the short form is natural, or to reverse the order: 他没来开会有事 is wrong.

examples.text: 你有问题可以随时问我。
examples.reading: nǐ yǒu wèntí kěyǐ suíshí wèn wǒ.
examples.translation: If you have any questions, you can ask me at any time.

examples.text: 她有车不开，每天骑自行车上班。
examples.reading: tā yǒu chē bù kāi, měi tiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.translation: She has a car but doesn't drive it; she cycles to work every day.

examples.reading: tā yǒu shì méi lái kāihuì.
examples.translation: He had something on, so he didn't come to the meeting.

examples.reading: yǒu kòng lái wǒ jiā wánr ba.
examples.translation: Come over to my place when you have time.

examples.reading: tā jiè le qián bù huán.
examples.translation: He borrowed money and won't pay it back.

examples.reading: tā zuò dìtiě qù jīchǎng.
examples.translation: He takes the underground to the airport.

lessons.title: A + Adj + B + amount: comparing without 比 (他大我三岁)
lessons.summary: With a short adjective such as 大, 小, 高, 早 or 晚, Chinese can compare without 比 by putting B right after the adjective and the exact difference at the end: 哥哥大我三岁.
pattern: A + 早 / 晚 + B + amount + V
body: The usual comparison is A 比 B + Adj + amount: 哥哥比我大三岁. A shorter pattern drops 比 and puts B straight after the adjective: 哥哥大我三岁 (my brother is three years older than me), 我高他五厘米, 弟弟小我两岁. With 早 and 晚 a verb phrase can follow: 他早我一年进公司, 妹妹晚我两年上大学.

The pattern works only with a few one-syllable adjectives of age, size, height or time (大, 小, 高, 矮, 早, 晚), and the amount at the end is required: 他大我 alone is not a sentence. B is usually a person or a pronoun.
The contrast example uses 比: 这个房间比那个大十平方米. With 比, B comes before the adjective; in the short pattern B comes after it. Do not use both at once.
A common mistake is to mix the two patterns: 他比大我三岁 is wrong; say 他比我大三岁 or 他大我三岁.

examples.reading: gēge dà wǒ sān suì.
examples.translation: My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ gāo tā wǔ límǐ.
examples.translation: I'm five centimetres taller than him.

examples.reading: tā zǎo wǒ yì nián jìn gōngsī.
examples.translation: He joined the company a year before me.

examples.reading: mèimei wǎn wǒ liǎng nián shàng dàxué.
examples.translation: My younger sister started university two years after me.

examples.reading: dìdi xiǎo wǒ liǎng suì.
examples.translation: My younger brother is two years younger than me.

examples.text: 这个房间比那个大十平方米。
examples.reading: zhège fángjiān bǐ nàge dà shí píngfāngmǐ.
examples.translation: This room is ten square metres bigger than that one.

lessons.title: 被 / 叫 / 让 + agent + 给 + V: passive sentences with 给
lessons.summary: In a colloquial passive sentence, 给 can stand right before the verb after 被, 叫 or 让 and the agent: 我的自行车让人给偷了; it stresses what happened to the subject.
pattern: subject + 被 / 叫 / 让 + agent + 给 + V + 了 / complement
body: Spoken passive sentences often add 给 just before the verb: 我的自行车让人给偷了, 那个杯子叫弟弟给打碎了, 衣服让雨给淋湿了. The meaning is the same as without 给, but 给 makes it sound more colloquial and stresses the effect on the subject, usually something unwelcome. The verb still needs something after it, such as 了 or a complement (打碎了, 拿走了).
被 can be used with or without an agent, but 叫 and 让 always need one: 杯子让弟弟给打碎了 is fine, 杯子让给打碎了 is not. Use 人 when you do not know who did it: 让人给偷了.
The contrast example uses 把: 他的话把妈妈给气哭了. 给 can also stand before the verb in a 把 sentence. There the subject is the cause or doer and the object after 把 is affected, the reverse of a passive.
A common mistake is to drop the agent after 叫 or 让, or to end with a bare verb: 自行车被人给偷 is unfinished; add 了.

examples.text: 我的自行车让人给偷了。
examples.reading: wǒ de zìxíngchē ràng rén gěi tōu le.
examples.translation: My bike got stolen.

examples.text: 那个杯子叫弟弟给打碎了。
examples.reading: nàge bēizi jiào dìdi gěi dǎsuì le.
examples.translation: That cup got broken by my little brother.

examples.text: 这件事被他给说出去了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì bèi tā gěi shuō chūqu le.
examples.translation: He let this slip to other people.

examples.reading: yīfu ràng yǔ gěi lín shī le.
examples.translation: My clothes got soaked by the rain.

examples.reading: nà běn shū bèi shéi gěi ná zǒu le?
examples.translation: Who took that book away?

examples.text: 他的话把妈妈给气哭了。
examples.reading: tā de huà bǎ māma gěi qì kū le.
examples.translation: What he said made Mum so upset she cried.

lessons.title: ……，便……: and then, straight away (formal 就)
lessons.summary: 便 in the second clause says the next action follows at once or naturally from the first; it is a more written, formal word for 就.
body: 便 (biàn) is an adverb that stands before the verb of the second part and says one thing follows the other directly: 他放下行李，便出去找朋友了, 她说完这句话，便离开了会场. It works like 就 but sounds more written; stories and reports use it often. Like 就, it can close an 一…… frame (一到冬天，这里便很少有人来) or a condition with 只要 (只要你多练习，便能说得流利).
便 is an adverb, so it goes after the subject of the second clause, never before it: 看完信，她便明白了一切, not 便她明白了.
The contrast example uses 然后: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影. 然后 is a linking word for the next step in a plan, often after 先, and it can stand before the subject; 便 stresses that the second action follows at once.
A common mistake is to pair 便 with 只有: 只有……才 is fixed, so 只有你多练习，便能…… is wrong; use 只要 with 便.

examples.text: 他放下行李，便出去找朋友了。
examples.reading: tā fàngxià xíngli, biàn chūqu zhǎo péngyou le.
examples.translation: He put down his bags and went straight out to see his friends.

examples.text: 她说完这句话，便离开了会场。
examples.reading: tā shuō wán zhè jù huà, biàn líkāi le huìchǎng.
examples.translation: Having said this, she left the hall.

examples.text: 一到冬天，这里便很少有人来。
examples.reading: yí dào dōngtiān, zhèlǐ biàn hěn shǎo yǒu rén lái.
examples.translation: Once winter comes, hardly anyone comes here.

examples.text: 只要你多练习，便能说得流利。
examples.reading: zhǐyào nǐ duō liànxí, biàn néng shuō de liúlì.
examples.translation: As long as you practise a lot, you will speak fluently.

examples.text: 看完信，她便明白了一切。
examples.reading: kàn wán xìn, tā biàn míngbai le yíqiè.
examples.translation: After reading the letter, she understood everything.

examples.text: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影。
examples.reading: wǒmen xiān chīfàn, ránhòu qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: We'll eat first and then go to the cinema.

lessons.title: 或是……，或是……: either … or … (in statements)
lessons.summary: 或是……，或是…… lists two possible actions or choices in a statement, a more formal version of 或者……，或者……; questions use 还是 instead.
pattern: S + 或是 + V1，或是 + V2
body: 或是 (huòshì) means or, like 或者, with a slightly more formal tone. Repeated at the head of two clauses it says one or the other happens: 周末我或是在家看书，或是去公园散步. It can also join two phrases once: 你可以发邮件或是打电话告诉我. The two choices are equal, so they can usually change places.
或是 belongs to statements. In a question that asks the listener to choose, use 还是: 你到底去还是不去? That is the contrast example: 还是 asks, 或是 states the options.
The two parts of 或是……，或是…… should be parallel, with the same kind of phrase after each 或是 (two verb phrases, or two people: 或是你去办，或是我去办).
A common mistake is to use 或是 in a choice question: 你喝茶或是喝咖啡? is wrong when you ask someone to choose; say 你喝茶还是喝咖啡?

examples.text: 周末我或是在家看书，或是去公园散步。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ huòshì zài jiā kàn shū, huòshì qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.translation: At weekends I either read at home or go for a walk in the park.

examples.text: 遇到不懂的词，可以问老师或是查词典。
examples.reading: yùdào bù dǒng de cí, kěyǐ wèn lǎoshī huòshì chá cídiǎn.
examples.translation: When you meet a word you don't know, you can ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.

examples.text: 你可以发邮件或是打电话告诉我。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ fā yóujiàn huòshì dǎ diànhuà gàosu wǒ.
examples.translation: You can let me know by email or by phone.

examples.text: 这件事或是你去办，或是我去办。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì huòshì nǐ qù bàn, huòshì wǒ qù bàn.
examples.translation: Either you deal with this or I do.

examples.reading: nǐ dàodǐ qù háishi bú qù?
examples.translation: So are you going or not?

lessons.title: 一旦……就…… (once …) and 假如……（就）…… (if, supposing)
lessons.summary: 一旦……就…… says that once something happens, a consequence follows; 假如…… sets up a supposition, real or imagined, with 就 or a question in the second clause.
body: 一旦 (yídàn) means once or if ever: it introduces an event that may or may not happen and stresses that, once it does, the result follows and is hard to undo: 一旦做了决定，他就不会改变, 机会一旦错过，就不会再来了. The second clause usually has 就.

假如 (jiǎrú) means if or supposing, a slightly more formal 如果. It can introduce a real possibility (假如明天下雨，运动会就改到下周) or an imagined one (假如你能回到过去，你最想做什么?). 就 is common but can be left out, especially when the second clause is a question or has 会 or 不可能 (假如没有你的帮助，我不可能这么快完成).
The contrast example uses 只要: 只要你有时间，就来参加吧. 只要 states a sufficient condition (as long as), not a supposition or a risk. Like 一旦 and 假如 it pairs with 就; 只有 pairs with 才, so 只有……就 is wrong.
A common mistake is to use 一旦 for something that has already happened: say 因为他做了决定, not 一旦他做了决定 about a past fact.

lessons.title: 万一 (in case) and 要不然 / 不然 (otherwise)
lessons.summary: 万一…… raises an unlikely, usually unwelcome possibility (in case …); ……，要不然/不然…… says what will or would happen otherwise.
pattern: clause，要不然 / 不然 + (S) + (就) + result
body: 万一 (wànyī, literally one in ten thousand) introduces a possibility that is unlikely and usually unwelcome: 万一下雨，我们就在家看电影. It is common in advice and in questions about what to do: 多带点儿钱吧，万一不够怎么办? The second clause often has 就.

要不然 and its shorter form 不然 mean otherwise, or else. The first clause says what to do or what happened; the second, after 要不然 or 不然, says the result if that were not so: 快走吧，要不然就赶不上火车了, 你最好穿件外套，不然会感冒的. After a past fact it means otherwise … would have: 幸亏你提醒我，要不然我就忘了.
The contrast example uses 既然: 既然你已经决定了，就去做吧. 既然 (since, now that) starts from a fact both people accept, while 万一 imagines something that has not happened and probably will not.
A common mistake is to use 然后 for otherwise: 快走吧，然后就赶不上火车了 says the opposite of what you mean.

examples.text: 万一下雨，我们就在家看电影。
examples.reading: wànyī xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù zài jiā kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: If it happens to rain, we'll stay home and watch a film.

lessons.title: ……，因而…… (and so) and ……，可见…… (which shows that)
lessons.summary: 因而 opens the second clause with a result that follows from the first, in a formal style; 可见 opens a conclusion drawn from the facts in the first clause.
body: 因而 (yīn'ér) means therefore, and so. It stands at the start of the second clause and introduces the result of the cause in the first: 他每天坚持锻炼，因而身体一直很好. It is more formal than 所以 and, unlike 所以, it is not paired with 因为 at the start of the sentence.

可见 (kějiàn) means which shows that, so clearly. The first clause states a fact; the second, after 可见, is the speaker's conclusion from it: 大家都来参加了，可见这个活动很受欢迎. The direction is fact, then conclusion, not cause, then result.
The contrast example uses 因为……所以……: 因为路上堵车，所以他迟到了. 因为 opens the cause clause at the front; 因而 and 可见 only open the second clause, so 因而路上堵车 is wrong.
A common mistake is to put the reason after 可见: 他没来，可见他生病了 is a conclusion; if you know he is ill, say 他生病了，所以没来.

examples.text: 他每天坚持锻炼，因而身体一直很好。

examples.text: 大家都来参加了，可见这个活动很受欢迎。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu lái cānjiā le, kějiàn zhège huódòng hěn shòu huānyíng.

examples.text: 因为路上堵车，所以他迟到了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lù shang dǔchē, suǒyǐ tā chídào le.
examples.translation: He was late because of the traffic jam.

lessons.title: 哪怕……，也……: even if …, still …
lessons.summary: 哪怕 introduces an extreme or unlikely supposition, and 也 in the second clause says the result does not change: 哪怕下大雨，他也会去跑步.
pattern: 哪怕 + extreme supposition，S + 也 + V
body: 哪怕 (nǎpà) means even if. It sets up a supposition, often an extreme one, and the second clause says the outcome stays the same; 也 stands before its verb: 哪怕只有一点儿希望，我们也不能放弃. It is close to 即使 and 就算 but more colloquial and more emphatic. 再 + adjective often follows it: 哪怕再忙.
The subject can come before 哪怕 when both clauses share it: 我哪怕不睡觉，也要把这本书看完. 也 stays after any time word or subject in the second clause: 她每天也要给妈妈打个电话.
The contrast example uses 虽然……但是……: 虽然这家饭馆有点儿贵，但是我们还是常来. 虽然 concedes a real fact (the restaurant really is expensive); 哪怕 imagines a case that may not happen. So 哪怕 does not go with 但是.
A common mistake is to use 就 instead of 也: 哪怕下雨，他就会去 is wrong; even if needs 也 (or 都).

examples.text: 哪怕下大雨，他也会去跑步。
examples.reading: nǎpà xià dà yǔ, tā yě huì qù pǎobù.
examples.translation: Even if it pours with rain, he'll still go running.

examples.translation: Even if nobody else understands, I'll stick to my choice.

examples.text: 虽然这家饭馆有点儿贵，但是我们还是常来。

examples.translation: Although this restaurant is a bit expensive, we still come here often.

lessons.title: 不但不……，反而…… (not only not …, but instead) and 不是只……，还…… (not only … but also)
lessons.summary: 不但不 / 不但没有……，反而…… says that instead of the expected result, the opposite happened; 不是（只）……，还 / 还是…… says that something goes further than the first part claims.
pattern: S + 不但不 / 不但没(有) + V，反而 + opposite
S + 不是 (只) + A，还 / 还是 + B
body: 不但不 (or 不但没有 for a past event) denies the expected result, and 反而 (fǎn'ér, on the contrary) gives the opposite one: 吃了药，他的病不但没有好，反而更重了, 我帮了他，他不但不感谢，反而生气了. 反而 is an adverb, so it goes after any subject in the second clause.

不是……，还…… goes in the other direction: the first part is true but not the whole story, and the second adds more. It is most natural with 只 or 光: 她不是只会唱歌，还会跳舞. When the second part names what the person also is, it takes 还是, that is 还 plus 是 (hái shì, also is): 我爸爸不是只会工作，还是个很好的厨师.

The contrast example uses 不但……而且……: 他不但会做饭，而且做得很好吃. 而且 adds something in the same direction; 反而 is used only when the second part goes against what the first led you to expect, and only after a negative 不但不 / 不但没.
A common mistake is to use 反而 after a positive 不但: 他不但会做饭，反而做得很好吃 is wrong; use 而且.

examples.text: 雨不但没停，反而越下越大了。
examples.reading: yǔ búdàn méi tíng, fǎn'ér yuè xià yuè dà le.

examples.translation: He can not only cook, but cook really well.

lessons.title: ……，为的是……: the reason is to …, all in order to …
lessons.summary: 为的是 opens the second clause and states the purpose of the action in the first: 我们提前出发，为的是避开早高峰.
body: 为的是 (wèi de shì) means the purpose is, it is in order to. First you say what someone does, then, after a comma, 为的是 gives the goal: 他每天早起，为的是能多学一会儿, 妈妈这么做，为的是让你少走弯路. It puts weight on the purpose, often to explain or justify an action.
为的是 is fixed: the three syllables do not change (not 为得是 or 为了是), and it always opens the second clause, after the action.
The contrast example uses 为了: 为了能早点儿到，我们打了一辆车. 为了 usually comes first and gives the purpose before the action; 为的是 comes second. So 为的是 does not start a sentence.
A common mistake is to use 因为是 for purpose: 因为 gives a reason (a cause), 为的是 a goal.

examples.text: 他每天早起，为的是能多学一会儿。
examples.reading: tā měi tiān zǎo qǐ, wèi de shì néng duō xué yíhuìr.

examples.text: 我们提前出发，为的是避开早高峰。
examples.reading: wǒmen tíqián chūfā, wèi de shì bìkāi zǎo gāofēng.
examples.translation: We set off early to avoid the morning rush hour.

examples.text: 妈妈这么做，为的是让你少走弯路。

examples.translation: We took a taxi so we could get there a bit earlier.

lessons.title: Compressed sentences: 没有……就没有……, 不……不……, 再……也……
lessons.summary: Some two-clause meanings are packed into one short sentence: 没有A就没有B (without A there is no B), 不A不B (unless A, not B), and 再Adj也V (however …, still …).
pattern: 没有 + A + (，) 就没有 + B
不 + V1 + 不 + V2 / 不行
再 + Adj / V + 也 + V
body: A compressed sentence (紧缩复句) is a complex sentence with the comma and most linking words removed. 没有A就没有B says A is the condition for B: 没有大家的帮助，就没有我今天的成功, 没有你就没有这个家.

不A不B is a double negative meaning unless A, not B, or if not A, then not B: 他不做完作业不睡觉 (he won't go to bed until his homework is done). 不V不行 means must: 这个问题不解决不行. The set phrase 不见不散 (see you there, we wait until we meet) is built the same way.

再A也B means however A, still B: 工作再忙也要按时吃饭, 这件衣服再便宜我也不买. 再 here does not mean again; with an adjective it means no matter how. The contrast example uses 就 alone: 你想去就去吧, a compressed condition (if you want to go, go), where 就 joins the two verbs with no 再 or 也.
A common mistake is to replace the second 不 with 没: 他不做完作业没睡觉 is wrong; the frame is 不……不…… .
